steps.text: Wasserland, Leithanien

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: How do you like this piece?

steps.name: Lateran Cleric
steps.text: Like an energetic child waking from slumber, rushing out the door to enjoy the fruits of life to the fullest.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: It was the Kurfürst who wrote it, inspired by His Holiness's visit to Wasserland when he was still a Messenger for Laterano.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: The young and enthusiastic future pontiff told the children about all that he has seen... the ocean that Iberia watches over, the city of Athenius, where Minoan myth and machination exist in equal measure.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: And... a passing mention of Kazdel, the city of sin, the whereabouts of which are unknown.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: The Kurfürst was there, and he was fascinated by His Holiness's descriptions.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: The first draft of this work was in fact written at that time, but the Kurfürst was not satisfied. Even after many years of revisions, a final draft has yet to be completed...

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: Until recently, when our scouts located the elusive nomadic city of the devils and sent back photos.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: Gazing upon the enormous tracks left behind by the city, the Kurfürst found the missing element in the music—ferocity. With that, the work was complete.

steps.name: Lateran Cleric
steps.text: You found Kazdel?

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: Yes. The Kurfürst was astonished to find that the destiny of the work was intertwined with the city's.

steps.name: Lateran Cleric
steps.text: I understand the reason the Kurfürst chose to present this piece on the eve of my return to Laterano.

steps.name: Lateran Cleric
steps.text: However, unlike his predecessors, His Holiness has no intention of initiating offensive action against the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Lateran Cleric
steps.text: He is not interested in putting the sinless on trial without cause. I'm afraid I must disappoint the Kurfürst.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: The city itself is of no concern to the Kurfürst. He is far more interested in His Holiness's opinion of the piece.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: Please send His Holiness the Kurfürst's warmest regards.

steps.name: Courier
steps.text: We have a response from Siracusa. Only a few of the famiglie have agreed to participate in the action. Their men will rendezvous with the fleet soon.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: I can't believe Laterano rejected us... Inform the Siracusans to move quickly. We must mop up the city before the other kreise can react.

steps.name: Amiable Official
steps.text: Take Kazdel before the other Kurfürsten can. Do not repeat the mistake we made at Gaul and miss another opportunity.
Scar Market, Kazdel

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I like Leithanians. You always bring so much business.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: And it's smart that you disguised yourself as a prisoner in a smuggling crew, rather than flying the banner of a Messenger.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Now tell me what you want, before I lose my patience.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Trade, muscle for hire, intel... The Scar Market has everything you need.

steps.name: Nervous Envoy
steps.text: Cooperation, esteemed leader.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: We don't have a fixed price for 'cooperation'.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Are you sure your Kurfürst can pay my price?

steps.name: Nervous Envoy
steps.text: Don’t you want to know what we're asking for first?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: There's nothing that money cannot buy here, Caprinae.

steps.name: Nervous Envoy
steps.text: What about Kazdel?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: ...Go on.

steps.name: Nervous Envoy
steps.text: The Kurfürst wants you to sabotage the city's propulsion system, nothing else.

steps.name: Nervous Envoy
steps.text: The down-payment is in the safe that you took from the caravan.

steps.name: Nervous Envoy
steps.text: The Kurfürst will discuss the rest of the payment with you in Kazdel.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I admire your boldness. Let me express my good faith with a little glimpse into the future for you.
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: Take your things and scram, Leithanian! Are you trying to poison me?

steps.name: Dejected Babel Member
steps.text: These are just suppressants. You'll need them on the battlefield...

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: The warships that surround us came from Leithanien!

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: Outsiders like you must have led them here!

steps.name: Dejected Babel Member
steps.text: I... I don't have an explanation. I know you're taking your son with you into battle. He could use the medicine—

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: Keep your hands off my son!

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: What's the commotion—are you out of your mind? She's a Babel doctor!

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Are you okay?

steps.name: Dejected Babel Member
steps.text: I'm fine. He wasn't really trying to hurt me.

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: Hmph. Goodluck.

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: You married a Babel woman, and now you've become a shill for the invaders? They'll be the death of you, I guarantee it.

steps.name: Dejected Babel Member
steps.text: Many of us are also pained by the impending war...

steps.name: Dejected Babel Member
steps.text: We've requested to join you on the frontlines.

steps.name: Angry Sarkaz
steps.text: Lunatics... who knows what schemes you have on the frontline... you'll get yours in the end...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Give me the medicine. I'll distribute it.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: They're ready to leave. Go meet up with them. I'll take care of things here.

steps.name: Dejected Babel Member
steps.text: Goodluck, your son...

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: I didn't let him leave.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: If the Leithanians want to force us into a Catastrophe, it's safer for him to be in the lower-level shelters in the city.

steps.name: Goodluck
steps.text: Relax, doctor. People have made it through Catastrophes in the past. Maybe we'll have, you know, good luck!
The furnace has burned for more than a century.
War, Catastrophe, migration, exile... all the suffering since the Teekaz era has not extinguished the hatred of the revenants.
The Sarkaz have seen many Kazdels through the ages. The memory of yesterday may be unrecognizable by tomorrow...
But the Soul Furnace has been a constant for this generation of Sarkaz.
Home is where the Soul Furnace is.
Kazdel.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The furnace has not burned like this for many years. I can hear the cries of the revenants even from here.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Soon, this city will charge headlong into a Catastrophe...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: All we need to do is hold out until Nezzsalem's reinforcements arrive, until Kazdel once again passes through the Catastrophe—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They thought we would cower. They tried to assume our thoughts with their conception of common sense. It was so a hundred and seventy years ago, and it is so now.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Arrogant and laughable fools who never took the time to truly understand us.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What fate do you think awaits this city, Theresis?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: To be honest, the chances that it survives are slim.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Kazdel was immobilized the last time it braved a Catastrophe. It took us a decade just to get it moving at full speed again.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And the forests of crystals in the mines and on the walls could never be removed, ruining years of our plans for the city.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I don't know if the city can survive another ordeal like that, much less one that's even worse. Good luck rarely comes twice.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I believe in this city, Theresis.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Not because of luck, but because we built this city, and I won't give up on it.
The story of this city does not end here, Your Highness.
I may not be able to see its future clearly, but there is one thing I can say for sure—the city continues to exist into the distant future.
No one can say, however, if it will be a sanctuary of hope, or a ghost city of the dead.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Scareye... have you not grown tired of the ambiguous words of your kind?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And need I remind you that no amount of mercenaries can ensure your safety in this city.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: There is no deceiving Your Highnesses, of course.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kazdel's doors are open to every Sarkaz, but you'd better have a good reason to set foot in this city with your mercenaries at a time like this.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I was made an offer most difficult to refuse, which obliged me to enter the city to seek an audience.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What is that you're carrying?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: This? Something insignificant. Oh, I mean someone. The Leithanians wanted me to sabotage Kazdel.

spans.text: This? Something insignificant. Oh, I mean some
. The Leithanians wanted me to sabotage Kazdel.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: I have been away from my kin for many years, but as your Highness said, Kazdel is the root of all Sarkaz.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: So, I felt that I had to deliver this Leithanian with my own hands, in order to prove my innocence.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What are you thinking?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Exactly as I have said. What can I possibly hide before the King of Sarkaz?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: But if you're not interested in my gift of good faith, then I see no need to carry it with me anymore. It's heavy, after all.
He casually casts the bag into the furnace, where it is incinerated in an instant.
Without a sound.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: The furnace is always an impressive sight, no matter how many times one sees it.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Your Highness need not pity him. He should have foreseen the risks when he approached the Scar Market.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I trust Leithanien was not miserly with its terms.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It's simple, Your Highness. I prefer immediate payment over empty promises. But more importantly, I don't work with the losing side.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Are you predicting our victory?

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: It wasn't I who saw it. It was the Cyclops who left the prophecy a thousand years ago. I'm simply betting that Your Highnesses are the protagonists of the prophecy.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Regardless, the safest business for the Scar Market is with Your Highnesses. It would keep business flowing for at least the next fifty years or so.

steps.name: Scareye
steps.text: Is that not so, Your Highnesses?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You're clever. Prophecy doesn't bring victory, but we can. Bring your mercenaries. We're moving out.
The crowd stirs.
The Sarkaz procession leaving the city is quiet, except for the occasional clang of weapons and equipment.
Their silence is rooted in the knowledge of the fate that awaited them beyond the city’s gates.
They wrap banners, torn from the walls, around their waists, or clutch Originium spikes, chopped from the streets, as makeshift weapons...
Each has their own ritual to remember the city that they may never return to.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Mom... Dad, where are you?

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Dad! Mom!

steps.name: Indifferent Woman
steps.text: Hmph... people really need to watch their kids. They can’t be allowed to run wild.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Ouch...

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Careful.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Th-Thank you.

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Where did you come from? Why are you also leaving the city? You'll fall if you’re not careful.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: I'm looking for my mom and dad. Are you going out, too?

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Yes... I'm going to the battlefield.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Are you looking for your mom and dad there, too? Can I come with you?

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: No... I'm by myself.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Why are you going out, then?

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Because I don't want to hide in the city. I want to fight the people who are doing bad things to us. That's what my parents told me before they... they left.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: I... I want to fight, too, but Mom and Dad won't let me go. I tried to sneak out and got a beating when they found out. But I don't want to be away from Mom and Dad.

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: We'll go together then, and find your mom and dad. But there'll be a lot of bad people out there. Are you scared?

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: You're not scared. Mom and Dad aren't scared. I'm not scared either!
The disheveled child pumps his fists to show courage, but his trembling betrays him.
The older child knows that the young boy does not fully understand what is happening outside the city.
But the young boy knows something simple but true.
Bad guys should be chased away. Families should stay together. So he takes the boy's hand, and joins the procession.

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: How do we find your parents when we're out there?

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: They work for Babel. They have a picture of a tower on their clothes.

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Babel. I know that place.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Are you from Babel too?

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: No, I grew up in a Military Commission institution. I guess I'm from the Military Commission.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Military Commission? What's that?

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: A place that protects people, just like Babel.

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: What's your dad's name? Let's squeeze our way to the front. Maybe they're up ahead.

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Goodluck!

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Good luck?

steps.name: Lost Child
steps.text: Yes, he's Goodluck... why are you laughing?

steps.name: Brave Child
steps.text: Nothing... let's shout his name. Maybe he'll hear you!
Two children squeeze forward in the procession, holding each other's hand, calling out 'Goodluck' with their tiny voices.
A few heads turn, and sigh when they see the young and naive faces.
Good luck.
It is what they all need.
On an evening in the autumn of 1068, the music playing in the Kurfürst of Wasserland's study was interrupted by the sound of frantic knocking on the door.
The fleet that was pursuing the nomadic city of Kazdel had broken off its pursuit.
'Those crazy devils charged straight into a Catastrophe. It's only by sheer good luck that they got away.'
Years later, the Kurfürst of Wasserland still recounted the reason for his failure with palpable disdain.
